_meta.what: A third number, next to capacity and house, and the only one design.md should quote at a generator.
_meta.why: capacity is what the geometry holds and house is what a real deck sets. Neither is safe to hand to a model that writes the content: it cannot see the rendered page and gets no signal when a block crosses its floor. The snapshot page is the case that forced this. Its house content equals its capacity at 9 bullet lines, and one extra line break used to overflow it by 23px against 0.7px of slack.
_meta.rule: budget = min(house, capacity - 1). One item of headroom against the geometry limit, and never more than a real deck sets. Where a count is fixed by the grid rather than by density (three panels, three stat columns) the budget equals it, because there is no such thing as two and a half columns.
_meta.measured: 2026-07-28, by research/tools/capacity.py, after the bullet leading came to the record's 1.20x and the inter-bullet gap to its 1.28x. Every one of these goes stale the moment the length of the item counted changes. Re-run the tool, do not edit this file by hand.
_meta.reading: Each count is 'of the item as written on that slide'. The split page holds 13 of the two-line bullets it actually sets and would hold roughly twice as many one-line ones. A count means nothing without the size of the thing counted.
